title: [Workshop] AI Pipelines and Agents in Pure TypeScript with Mastra.ai — Nick Nisi, Zack Proser
talk_summary: A Mastra.ai workshop building a meme generator in TypeScript, demonstrating typed multi-step workflows (Zod-validated steps with data mapping), agents that call workflows, and a local playground for step-level debugging.

takeaways.what_they_do: Because each workflow step is a discrete unit, they assign different models per step: cheap/fast models for simple extraction, stronger models only where needed, even tiny models on Cloudflare Workers for trivial steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: extracting frustrations is like that's pretty simple and should be fast and cheap. So it's like do 40 or even something simpler or maybe even get away with like a seven billion parameter model

takeaways.technique: Deterministic workflow instead of agent-decided tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that giving an LLM many tools and letting it choose is unreliable; encoding the sequence as a fixed workflow with typed steps and data mapping gives determinism, and the agent just invokes the workflow as one callable unit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you give something a 100 tools and then ask an LLM like you've got 100 tools. Let's like go to Disneyland. I don't know exactly what we're going to get out of that

takeaways.technique: Zod schema validation + coercion at step boundaries
takeaways.what_they_do: Every step declares input/output Zod schemas; runtime validation coerces types and catches non-conforming LLM output, and they added a structured-output compatibility layer after testing 30 schemas across 16 models because models silently violate constraints like string length.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the models don't always actually respect the schemas that you give them ... we added like a tool compatibility structured output layer that reduced that like reduce the error rate a lot

takeaways.technique: MCP docs server to eliminate hallucinated API usage
takeaways.what_they_do: Installing the framework's MCP doc server into the coding assistant gave it current docs, which they credit with near-zero hallucinations and one-shot correct feature implementations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that session where I coded um there were zero hallucinations and so that means that every time I asked for a feature it was oneshotted. correctly

takeaways.technique: Step-level local playground debugging before full runs
takeaways.what_they_do: The dev playground lets them run and inspect input/output of each workflow step individually, tweak prompts/temperature/model per request, and iterate locally without deploying or running the whole pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can just iterate locally, change the prompts, change the schemas until you get it exactly the way you want and then you haven't wasted time going back and forth

takeaways.technique: Baked-in pipeline evals as health metric
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite evals as the production practice for knowing whether a pipeline is healthy, and note OpenAI's recommendation to start with an evaluated pipeline; Mastra ships eval primitives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: people that are actually in prod are using evaluations to determine the health of their pipeline and the health of each individual generation
